summary: The S&P 500 closed at 7,677.28, up 0.32% on the day, with the Nasdaq 100 adding 0.62% as technology reclaimed leadership ahead of NVIDIA's earnings report Wednesday. The 10 year yield held at 4.64%, down 1.38%, while TLT gained 1.10% to 83.47 as oil dropped another 4.18% to 81.46 on diplomatic signals around Iran and the Strait of Hormuz, extending the bond friendly trend from yesterday. Gold pushed higher to 4,720.60, up 1.72%, copper gained 1.69%, and Bitcoin settled at 78,851.51, essentially flat, as the hard asset and debasement trade remained in force. Consumer confidence came in at 90.3, missing the forecast of 100.0 and sitting at its lowest level in seven months, with gas above 4 dollars per gallon cited as a drag. Asian markets were the notable weak spot, with KOSPI falling 3.12% and the Hang Seng dropping 1.89%, while European bourses gained modestly after German GDP and business sentiment beat expectations. The week's defining moments are still ahead: NVIDIA reports after the close Wednesday, Core PCE and preliminary GDP also arrive Wednesday, and Fed Chair Warsh speaks at Jackson Hole on Friday.
